keeps.name: Jesse Owens State Park - Sand Hollow Campground
keeps.waterfront_evidence: ODNR campground page ('borders Horse Run Lake... Several sites border the lake') + Ohio OSIP leaf-off imagery (0.3 m) of the gravel road up the east shore: drive-in spurs ~18 m from the waterline at 39.7368,-81.7331 and ~16 m at 39.7393,-81.7339; USGS 3DEP spot heights put those spurs ~3-4 m above the 257.4 m pool, an easy walk down, not a bluff (the pull-off at 39.7420,-81.7343 is ~8 m up, steep). Upstream of the dam at the lake's south end. Only some sites: the road runs on ~2.5 km and north of the lake sites are inland.
keeps.inclusion_evidence: ODNR lists Sand Hollow as a no-fee drive-in primitive campground and gives no length. Camper reports: 26-ft trailer at site 43 (Campendium 2021), 36-ft fifth wheel (Campendium 2020), 22-ft trailer at site 84 (Campendium 2024). A 23-ft motorhome fits at some sites, not all; ground is unlevel.
keeps.note: The northern no-fee area of the park: a gravel road up the east shore of Horse Run Lake and on into the woods, with sites strung along about 2.5 km. Some sit at the water; the far ones are a long walk from it (a 2022 Campendium reviewer at site 81 puts it at about 1.5 miles). Boat ramp at the south end of the lake. Former AEP ReCreation Land. ODNR gives no length; a 2021 Campendium reviewer with a 26-ft trailer found the sites 'very unlevel'. --Claude

sites.note: ODNR gives no site count or length and says 'no pad'. Camper reports only: about 82 sites (Dyrt 2024), numbered at least to 84. 26-ft trailer at site 43 (Campendium 2021: 'very unlevel. Suited mostly for tents, vans and very small campers'), 22-ft trailer at site 84 (Campendium 2024), 21-ft Class B at 50-51 (Campendium 2021), 36-ft fifth wheel (Campendium 2020). Pick a site on arrival; not all suit a 23-ft motorhome.

facilities.note: Latrines and a shelter house; picnic table and fire ring at each site. ODNR's region map also marks a spigot, while its campground page says no water, so bring water.

season.note: ODNR: 'generally April 1 to mid-December'; the close date is that wording, not a posted date.

booking.note: No-fee, first come, first served; campers self-register on site.

adds.name: Jesse Owens State Park - Big Muskie and Sawmill Road Campgrounds
adds.waterfront_evidence: ReserveOhio per-site coordinates plotted on Esri and Ohio OSIP leaf-off frames at 39.7362,-81.6862: Big Muskie's pads are in woods, nearest water a narrow pond ~55 m south of the nearest pad behind a tree belt, with no site on it. Sawmill Road's pads have no coordinates; its road runs a wooded valley with no water shown at it.
adds.inclusion_evidence: ReserveOhio per-site data: Big Muskie 48 listed sites, all RV, rated 39-75 ft (ODNR says 50); Sawmill Road 16 RV-typed of 29, 15 rated 26-70 ft. 65 public sites take 23 ft by ODNR's count.
adds.note: The park's two reservable campgrounds, about 300 m apart across a wooded ridge on neighbouring roads off the same highway: Big Muskie with full hookups and a store, and Sawmill Road, gravel primitive sites with a shower house. No water at the sites. --Claude

sites.note: Big Muskie: 50 full-hookup sites per ODNR, 1-50; ReserveOhio lists 48 (not 14 or 43), rated 39-75 ft, 11 pull-through (01, 02, 03, 08, 12, 18, 24, 36, 44, 45, 50). Sawmill Road: 15 RV-typed sites rated 23 ft or longer: 51, 52, 53, 57, 63, 65, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71 (30 ft), 72 (26 ft), 73, 79, 80; 63 and 65 pull-through. RV-typed 74 has no length and is not counted; the other 13 are tent-typed.

facilities.note: Shower house and flush restrooms at Big Muskie, with a store nearby. Sawmill Road has a shower house and no hookups.

booking.note: Big Muskie requires reservations, up to six months ahead online or at (866) 644-6727. Sawmill Road is reservable.

fees.note: $25 a night at Sawmill Road (no hookups; $24 off-peak); full hookups at Big Muskie $50 all year. Plus tax and the reservation fee. ReserveOhio's prices read 2026-10-31.

adds.name: Jesse Owens State Park - Hook Lake Campground
adds.waterfront_evidence: Ohio OSIP leaf-off frames at 39.7245,-81.7100 and 39.7263,-81.7082: the pin's gravel road with the tables and archery lot has no water within ~300 m; the upper loop's vehicles (39.7293,-81.7060) sit ~45 m from a pond behind brush; the youth pond is ringed by a paved day-use road, shelter and playground; the lake west of SR 83 is across the highway. Pads within 25 m of water not shown; default down.
adds.inclusion_evidence: ODNR lists Hook Lake as a no-fee primitive campground and gives no length. Campendium 2025-07-14: 'only a few pull-throughs big enough for our 34 foot motorhome, but we fit just fine'; Dyrt 2024-10-09: a 40+ ft rig on a hill site; Campendium 2020: 33-ft trailer level at site 27.
adds.note: A no-fee area at the east end of the park, off SR 83, around two ponds; the youth-only (15 and under) fishing ponds give it its name, with an archery range at the far end of the gravel road. A 2025 Campendium reviewer reports fitting a 34-ft motorhome; ODNR gives no length. A 2021 reviewer found the upper loop tight and points bigger rigs to the archery end, which is where this is pinned. --Claude

sites.note: ODNR gives no site count or length and says 'no pad'. Camper reports only: gravel, a little uneven, a few pull-throughs (Campendium 2025); numbered at least to 27. The upper loop is 'very tight' for a 40-ft fifth wheel, the archery-range area the one to use (Campendium 2021).

facilities.note: Multiple latrines, shelter houses, archery range; picnic table and fire ring at each site. ODNR's region map also marks a spigot, while its campground page says no water, so bring water.

season.note: ODNR: 'generally April 1 to mid-December'; the close date is that wording, not a posted date.

booking.note: No-fee, first come, first served; campers self-register on site.

adds.name: Jesse Owens State Park - Maple Grove Campground
adds.waterfront_evidence: Ohio OSIP leaf-off frame at 39.7068,-81.7247: small gravel loop east of SR 284, nearest water a lake arm ~170 m west across the highway.
adds.inclusion_evidence: ODNR lists Maple Grove as a no-fee primitive campground and gives no length, so kept under the silent-agency rule. Weak: a gravel loop and roadside row on leaf-off imagery, a host on site (Dyrt 2024), 'only a few are level' (Dyrt 2021), and no report of a rig of 23 ft or more.
adds.note: The smallest no-fee area, in the south of the park off SR 284: a row of sites by the road and a short gravel loop in the pines. No water at the sites. No reviewer reports a rig of 23 ft or more here, and ODNR gives no length. --Claude

sites.note: ODNR gives no site count or length and says 'no pad'. Camper reports only: 12 sites, close together (Dyrt 2024), 'space is tight' and only a few level (Dyrt 2021). No reported rig length; the fit for 23 ft is unconfirmed.

facilities.note: A latrine; picnic table and fire ring at each site. ODNR's region map also marks a spigot, while its campground page says no water, so bring water.
